column1: # gates-executed.tsv — THE RECORDED EXPECTATION that scripts/check-gates-executed.py enforces.
# Every row is a test that MUST HAVE EXECUTED. Not "must compile", not "must be present in the
# tree" — must have appeared in libtest's own output, by name, with a status.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. On 2026-07-20 a commit about ML-KEM deleted an FFI binding that two
# committed dregg-circuit-prove tests imported. `cargo test --workspace` compiles every target
# before running any, so ZERO tests ran in that crate for five days — and every signal we had
# was satisfied by the ABSENCE of execution. The law-1 ratchet (AIR is authored in Lean, never
# hand-written in Rust) and all 23 Lean<->Rust emit-equality gates were dark the whole time.
# The expected set has to be RECORDED, not derived: a set inferred at runtime from the same
# source the accident removes will always agree that nothing was expected. That is the whole
# design. The checker additionally hardcodes the two floors — `law1_enforcement_gate` by name,
# and >= 23 emit gates — in reviewed CODE, so emptying this file is not a way to go green.
# COLUMNS (tab-separated; blank lines and '#' comments ignored):
#   crate      cargo package name; run as `cargo test -p <crate> --test <stem>`
#   test_path  the test's name AS LIBTEST PRINTS IT (module path included, e.g. `teeth::foo`)
#   expect     `run`     — must report `ok`. `ignored` or absent is RED.
#              `ignored` — an expensive probe armed elsewhere (armed-teeth.yml runs --ignored);
#                          it may report `ignored` or `ok`, but it may not VANISH.
# THE ARMED SET IS THE CRATE THAT WENT DARK. Every row today is `dregg-circuit-prove`: that is
# where the incident happened and where the two named critical sets live. The `crate` column is
# here so widening is an append, not a rewrite — other gate-shaped suites exist and are NOT yet
# armed by this file (circuit/tests/*_gate.rs, exec-lean/tests/*_gate.rs, turn/tests/*_gate.rs,
# turn-prover, zkoracle-prove, fhegg-fhe, teasting). Saying so is the point: an arming list that
# does not name what it leaves out reads like coverage it does not have.
# THE #! DIRECTIVES ARE THE RATCHET. They are cross-checked against the rows below, so trimming
# rows to make a smaller reality pass requires editing the number too — deliberate, and visible
# in a diff. They are not decoration.
# TO ADD A GATE: add the file, then append its rows and bump the counts. The checker requires
# the `*_emit_gate.rs` glob to EQUAL the emit-gate stems here IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, so a new gate
# nothing arms is RED — a hand-kept arming list that can only lag does not go red, it quietly
# covers less, which is exactly how gates go dark.
# Counted 2026-07-25 against HEAD: 24 binaries, 23 emit gates, 191 tests.
